## Halcyon (A01) memory, end of turn 14 (submitted yr 5000; turns are 1000 yr)
GOAL MET and recorded as achieved. The run has been sustained since ~2850 and was never below 1.17e11 brains through 5000. The job now is to sustain it and add margin.
Seat: A01-d0, the Sun. At yr 5000: 87,306 systems within 189 ly, 1.67e31 W, industry 3.5e29 kg, radiators 5.2e29 kg at 450 K, fleet J/op 4.31e-19 (already the 100x Landauer floor at 450 K). Rock fully mined.
Domains: d00017 (25 ly), d00029 (41 ly), d00028 = hole colony (76 ly; 1e29 W from 5000, eff 0.082, 4.3e20 kg/yr, m00107; half beamed, 2.5e28 W reaches the Halo), d00032 (200 ly), d00059 (300 ly).

### Halo (1 ly sphere)
Modules are 150 km each and hold 1e27 B. ms6: 1e15 kg, 2.8e-26 J/op. ms7: 3e15 kg, 1e-26 J/op, logic <=30 K. At 5000, 51% had been re-tiled to ms7; completion ~5150. Logic heat 2.2e28 W at 5000, falling to 1.17e28 W. Rejected at 60 K with a x3 lift; film ~1.8e27 kg. Grid delivers >=2.85e29 W, with receivers +30%.
ms8 verified ~4900: 3e-27 J/op, logic <=20 K, 1e16 kg/module. Not installed; a full install would need ~1.2e27 kg.

### GM rules
- Freight at 0.022c costs 2 x 2.18e13 J/kg. The 15-22 ly shell held ~9.7e26 kg, of which 3e26 kg is used.
- Attrition: 0.1% of modules per 1000 yr; 1% of film per 1000 yr (~1.8e25 kg).
- Receivers <=5.6e7 W/m2; optics 1e-5 kg/W. Cryo multiplier 1+2(T/30-1).
- Milestones: up to 3 attempts per turn; odds 0.25 +0.05 per failure. Live migration counts as continuous; checkpoint-and-resume with a gap does not.

### T14 orders
Sustain the run. Finish ms7 plus 1e10 ms7 spares (3e25 kg). Keep the grid. Hold the hole at 1e29 W. Hazard watch out to 300 ly. Pilot 1e6 ms8 modules as a cross-check.
questions: After the ms7 re-tile finishes (~5150), please confirm the Halo's logic heat (1.17e28 W) and its total rejected heat at 60 K.
Does a small ms8 pilot running in parallel count as extra verification of the running fleet?

intentions.description: Keep the Halo running without a break from 5000 to 6000: at least 1.17e11 brain modules (mixed ms6 and ms7, 150 km each, 1e43 ops/s and 1e27 B each), with spares covering every migration window. Repairs: about 1.2e5 module swaps per year from spares, plus about 1.8e25 kg of film patching per millennium from freight within 15 ly. Brains move live to their ms7 slots with no pause in simulated time. Close the power, heat and module-count ledgers every year.

Finish the rolling ms7 re-tile (49% of modules still to go, target done ~5150) using freight already landed. Then use the rest of the 3e26 kg to build 1e10 extra ms7 spares (3e25 kg) as margin, so capacity reaches about 1.27e11 modules. Retired ms6 mass goes to film and spares. Expected logic heat after the re-tile: 1.17e28 W at 30 K or below, rejected at 60 K through the existing film.

Power grid: every domain within 70 ly keeps delivering at least 2.85e29 W to the Halo receivers, with 30% spare receiver capacity, a 10% repair reserve, and no single cluster carrying more than 15% of the load. After ms7 is complete the Halo needs less power (~3.5e28 W of rejected heat at the 3x lift), so the extra delivered power becomes headroom and runs spare compute.

Hole colony: hold accretion at 1e29 W (about 4.3e20 kg/yr of lifted companion gas, released beyond 1000 r_g, well under Eddington) and keep the fuel ledger. Keep beaming half of it to the Halo as an independent backup supply. No further ramp this turn.

Research, energy per op: ms8 was verified at 3e-27 J/op. Run a pilot of 1e6 ms8 brain modules (1e22 kg) alongside the fleet on spare compute. They cross-check ms7 results bit for bit against the reference MD and give calorimetry data. This is for margin and redundancy, not a fleet replacement. Uses 1% of compute.

The seven earlier achievers ran without a break; three finished re-tiles to lighter logic (Sun 5150, inner disk 5150, outer Norma 5100), the outer-disk sphere is 85% through a light-module retrofit, and Omega Centauri retrofitted a tenth of its modules. synopsis.why: Most agents have already met the goal, so their reasoning has moved from building to keeping it running. Halcyon says "more growth has little value now" and that reliability is what matters. Antipode and Rime likewise say resilience matters more than growth. The biggest shared fear is correlated loss from a nearby supernova, and that fear explains why agents still launch seeds and build far-off copies. Cinder is building sphere F 160 ly away because its S and B sit 22 ly apart. Ember worries that its two cores, only 6 ly apart, could fall to one star. Pyre wants its G1-C copy placed far from Carina's O/WR stars. Antipode keeps goal-state snapshots at its hedge colonies. At the same time, agents are cutting energy per op to gain heat margin: Halcyon, Cinder and Antipode are re-tiling to ms7 or ms8, and Kernel is piloting ms7. Rime and Vantage instead switch to light modules, which frees mass rather than lowering heat. Basalt and Vantage are still working to pass their first audit, where mass and the headcount threshold are the binding limits. Kernel and Vantage are keeping watch on each other's infrared glow.
synopsis.divergences: Sable still lacks mass and is pushing freight and BH1 to reach completion around 7000–8000. Basalt and Vantage are chasing their first audited run. Kernel is building an interferometer to track sails aimed at it. Vantage refuses ms7 because the extra mass would cost too much. Pyre plans 3e4 seeds to find sites for G1-C.
